title: 正弦电压加在电容上：i = C du/dt
statement: 电容 C = 100 µF 直接接在电压源上，u_s = 10 sin(100πt) V（已经持续很久）。电容电压、电流取关联参考方向（见图）。
求 t = 0 和 t = 1/150 s 时的电容电流 i_C，以及 t = 1/150 s 时电容吸收的瞬时功率 p_C。

questions.explain: i_C = C·du_C/dt = 100×10⁻⁶ × 10 × 100π·cos(100πt) = 0.1π·cos(100πt) A。t = 0 时 cos 0 = 1，i_C = 0.1π ≈ 0.3142 A——此刻电压为零，但变化最快，电流最大。

questions.ask: t = 1/150 s 时电容吸收的瞬时功率 p_C = ?
电容电流 i_C 与电压 u_C 的相位关系是：
questions.explain: u_C = 10 sin(100πt)，i_C = 0.1π cos(100πt) = 0.1π sin(100πt + 90°)，电流超前电压 90°。

hints: 电容电压就是电源电压 u_s，用 i_C = C·du_C/dt 求导。
瞬时功率 p = u·i（关联参考方向），可以为负。
solution: **1. 电流表达式。** 电容与电源并联，u_C = u_s = 10 sin(100πt) V。由 i_C = C du_C/dt：i_C = 10⁻⁴ × 10 × 100π cos(100πt) = **0.1π cos(100πt) A**（幅值 ≈ 0.3142 A）。
**4. 瞬时功率。** p_C = u_C·i_C = 8.660 × (−0.1571) ≈ **−1.360 W**。一般地 p_C = 0.5π·sin(200πt) W，在一个周期内正负各半：电容交替地吸收和释放能量，平均功率为零。
**5. 相位。** i_C 是 cos、u_C 是 sin，电流超前电压 90°——这是正弦稳态中电容的基本特征。

en.title: Sinusoidal voltage across a capacitor: i = C dv/dt
statement: A capacitor C = 100 µF is connected directly to a voltage source u_s = 10 sin(100πt) V (which has been running for a long time). The capacitor voltage and current follow the passive sign convention (see the drawing).
Find the capacitor current i_C at t = 0 and at t = 1/150 s, and the instantaneous power p_C absorbed by the capacitor at t = 1/150 s.

questions.explain: i_C = C·du_C/dt = 100×10⁻⁶ × 10 × 100π·cos(100πt) = 0.1π·cos(100πt) A. At t = 0, cos 0 = 1 and i_C = 0.1π ≈ 0.3142 A — the voltage is zero at this instant but changing fastest, so the current is at its maximum.
100πt = 2π/3 and cos(2π/3) = −0.5, so i_C = 0.1π × (−0.5) ≈ −0.1571 A. The voltage is falling, so the current is negative.

questions.ask: Instantaneous power absorbed by the capacitor at t = 1/150 s, p_C = ?
questions.explain: u_C = 10 sin(2π/3) = 8.660 V, p_C = u_C·i_C = 8.660 × (−0.1571) ≈ −1.360 W. p_C < 0: the capacitor is returning stored electric-field energy to the source.

questions.ask: The phase relation between i_C and u_C is:
questions.explain: u_C = 10 sin(100πt) and i_C = 0.1π cos(100πt) = 0.1π sin(100πt + 90°): the current leads the voltage by 90°.

hints: The capacitor voltage is the source voltage u_s; differentiate it using i_C = C·du_C/dt.
d/dt [sin(ωt)] = ω·cos(ωt), with ω = 100π rad/s here.
Instantaneous power is p = u·i (passive sign convention) and can be negative.
solution: **1. Current.** The capacitor is in parallel with the source, so u_C = u_s = 10 sin(100πt) V. From i_C = C du_C/dt: i_C = 10⁻⁴ × 10 × 100π cos(100πt) = **0.1π cos(100πt) A** (amplitude ≈ 0.3142 A).

**4. Instantaneous power.** p_C = u_C·i_C = 8.660 × (−0.1571) ≈ **−1.360 W**. In general p_C = 0.5π·sin(200πt) W, positive for half the time and negative for the other half: the capacitor alternately stores and returns energy, and its average power is zero.
**5. Phase.** i_C is a cosine and u_C a sine, so the current leads the voltage by 90° — the defining feature of a capacitor in sinusoidal steady state.
